hints: Draw a free-body diagram: the forces acting on $P$ are its weight $8g$ vertically downwards, the normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane, and the applied force of $100\text{ N}$ at angle $\theta$ above the inclined plane.
Resolve forces parallel to the plane: the uphill component of the applied force $100\cos\theta$ must balance the component of weight down the plane $8g\sin 30^\circ$.

Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane: the normal contact force $R$ balances the perpendicular component of weight plus the inward component of the pulling force: $R = 8g\cos 30^\circ + 100\sin\theta$.
walkthrough:
Since particle $P$ is in equilibrium on the smooth plane, resolve forces parallel to the line of greatest slope:
$$\Sigma F_{\parallel} = 0 \implies 100\cos\theta - 8g\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$100\cos\theta = 8(10)\sin 30^\circ = 80(0.5) = 40$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_{\perp} = 0 \implies R - 8g\cos 30^\circ - 100\sin\theta = 0$$
$$R = 8(10)\cos 30^\circ + 100\sin 66.4218^\circ$$

Calculate the normal reaction $R$ using $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.8660$ and $\sin 66.4218^\circ = \sqrt{1 - 0.4^2} = \sqrt{0.84} \approx 0.9165$:
$$R = 80(0.86603) + 100(0.91652) = 69.28 + 91.65 = 160.93 \approx 161\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition along the inclined plane:
$$\Sigma F_{\parallel} = 0$$
Taking the uphill direction as positive, the components along the plane are the forward component of the pulling force $100\cos\theta$ and the downward component of weight $mg\sin 30^\circ$:
$$100\cos\theta - mg\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$100\cos\theta = mg\sin 30^\circ$$

Substitute $m = 8\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$:
$$100\cos\theta = 8 \times 10 \times 0.5$$
$$100\cos\theta = 40$$
Divide both sides by $100$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{40}{100} = 0.4$$
Take the inverse cosine:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.4) = 66.4218^\circ \approx 66.4^\circ$$

State the equilibrium condition perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$\Sigma F_{\perp} = 0$$
Taking the normal away from the plane as positive, the forces perpendicular to the plane are $R$ outwards, the perpendicular component of weight $mg\cos 30^\circ$ inwards, and the perpendicular component of the pulling force $100\sin\theta$ inwards (pressing into the plane as shown in the diagram):
$$R - mg\cos 30^\circ - 100\sin\theta = 0$$
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ + 100\sin\theta$$

Substitute the known values:
$$R = 8 \times 10 \times \cos 30^\circ + 100\sin 66.4218^\circ$$
Compute each term:
$$80 \times \cos 30^\circ = 80 \times 0.866025 = 69.282\text{ N}$$
Since $\cos\theta = 0.4$, $\sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - 0.4^2} = \sqrt{0.84} \approx 0.916515$:
$$100 \times 0.916515 = 91.652\text{ N}$$
Add the two components:
$$R = 69.282 + 91.652 = 160.934 \approx 161\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves along plane to get $100\cos\theta = 8g\sin 30^\circ \implies \theta = 66.4^\circ$, and perpendicular to plane to get $R = 8g\cos 30^\circ + 100\sin\theta = 161\text{ N}$.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Resolves the applied $100\text{ N}$ force and weight parallel and perpendicular to the inclined surface.

hints: Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane: $F_{\text{net}} = ma$.
The forces acting along the line of greatest slope are the uphill component $100\cos 30^\circ$ and the downhill component of weight $8g\sin 30^\circ$.
Substitute $\theta = 30^\circ$, $m = 8\text{ kg}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into $100\cos 30^\circ - 8g\sin 30^\circ = 8a$ and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law, $F_{\text{net}} = ma$, parallel to the inclined plane in the uphill direction with $\theta = 30^\circ$:
$$100\cos 30^\circ - 8g\sin 30^\circ = 8a$$
$$100\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - 8(10)(0.5) = 8a$$
$$50\sqrt{3} - 40 = 8a$$

Evaluate the net force and solve for $a$:
$$86.6025 - 40 = 8a$$
$$46.6025 = 8a \implies a = \frac{46.6025}{8} \approx 5.83\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State Newton's second law for the particle along the line of greatest slope:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
Taking uphill as positive, the resultant force along the smooth plane is:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 100\cos\theta - mg\sin 30^\circ$$

Divide both sides by $8$ to determine $a$:
$$a = \frac{46.6025}{8} \approx 5.8253 \approx 5.83\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration is $5.83\text{ m s}^{-2}$ directed up the plane.
